rationale: C09 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. It closely matches the child's sequence: identification of the 1947 General Agreement and Proclamation No. 2761A; specification of a Schedule XX item and its concessionary duty treatment; a Tariff Commission finding of increased imports causing serious injury; a presidential finding that changing the concession is necessary to remedy that injury; invocation of section 350, section 7(c), and Article XIX; and an operative change effective after the close of business until otherwise proclaimed. The child adapts this machinery from modification of a concession to complete withdrawal and suspension. C01 and C13 are also strong escape-clause precedents but have less extensive literal correspondence with the child's opening and injury recitals.

shared_material.child_excerpt: under the authority vested in him by the Constitution and the statutes, including section 350 (a) ... on October 30, 1947, entered into a trade agreement ... [and] by Proclamation No. 2761A ... proclaimed such modifications of existing duties
shared_material.parent_excerpt: under the authority vested in him by the Constitution and the statutes, including section 350 (a) ... on October 30, 1947, entered into a trade agreement ... [and] by Proclamation No. 2761A ... proclaimed such modifications of existing duties
shared_material.explanation: The opening recital follows C09's language and organization almost verbatim.

shared_material.child_excerpt: in accordance with Article II ... and by virtue of the said Proclamation No. 2761A, the United States duty treatment ... reflects the duty concession granted
shared_material.parent_excerpt: in accordance with Article II ... and by virtue of the said Proclamation No. 2761A, the United States customs treatment ... reflects the concessions granted
shared_material.explanation: Both establish the existing concession through the same Article II and proclamation-based mechanism.

shared_material.parent_excerpt: the United States Tariff Commission has submitted to me its report of an investigation, including a hearing, under section 7 ... being imported ... in such increased quantities as to cause serious injury to the domestic industry producing like or directly competitive products
shared_material.explanation: This is distinctive shared language within the same ordered escape-clause finding.
